clue.text: Little Russians seen out after a girl

indicators.note: the shuffled word comes after the girl in the answer

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name

indicators.note: seen 'out' is seen put out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A group of small Russians has been spotted following a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SEEN into ENES, which follows RUTH. 'Little Russians' is an old name for Ukrainians and their neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthenians, once called Little Russians, are an East Slavic people of the Carpathians and Ukraine.

clue.text: Messy habits, perhaps ?

parts.note: not untidy ways but clothing worn in the military mess, habit being dress

explanation.surface: Someone has slovenly personal habits.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mess' is where service personnel eat, and a 'habit' is a garment, as a monk's.
explanation.definitionFit: Service personnel wear regulation dress in their mess, and a habit is a garment.

clue.text: Organ-players affections?

parts.note: the heart is an organ of the body
the strings are the players of stringed instruments in an orchestra

explanation.surface: Organists are fond of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ-players' suggests organists; split it into a body organ and orchestral players.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug at someone's heartstrings is to stir their deepest feelings of love or pity.

clue.text: Philanthropist gets amusement mounting racehorses, perhaps

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means going upwards, so the word for amusement is read bottom to top

parts.note: fun is amusement
the field is the set of horses running in a race

explanation.surface: A benefactor enjoys getting up on horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns FUN upwards to NUF. William Morris, Lord Nuffield, the car maker, founded the Nuffield Foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Nuffield, founder of Morris Motors, gave away vast sums to medicine and education.

clue.text: Southern European region is part of Asia.

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A southern European area is claimed to belong to Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast northern region of Russia in Asia.

clue.text: A hut the Ibo constructed

indicators.note: constructed means built, so the letters of the Ibo are put together anew

explanation.surface: Nigerian villagers have built themselves a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ibo (Igbo) are a people of Nigeria; 'constructed' rearranges THE IBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothie is a Scottish word for a rough cottage or shelter.

clue.text: Right man to get a rise

indicators.note: get a rise in a down clue means the name goes upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A worker is entitled to a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a rise' turns NEIL upwards. A lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim on property held as security for a debt.

clue.text: Doggedly continues' seeing PT school head about fresh rises

indicators.note: about means going round, so the physical-training letters enclose the rearranged word
fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of rises are rearranged
head picks the first letter of school

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going because the gym-class headmaster sees new promotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns RISES into ERSIS; 'about' puts PT round it, P-ERSIS-T, and 'head' adds S from 'school'. PT is physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to keep going stubbornly in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: King Edmund's field marshal

definitions.meaning: Edmund II of England carried the epithet as his byname
Edmund ..., British field marshal and Chief of the Imperial General Staff in 1939-40

explanation.surface: A king's title doubles as the name of a top army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anglo-Saxon king and the twentieth-century British field marshal shared the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The epithet of the eleventh-century English king was also the surname of a British field marshal of the Second World War.

clue.text: Eastern ruler returns this Epstein work

indicators.note: returns tells us to read the ruler's title backwards

parts.note: an amir or emir is a Muslim prince or ruler

explanation.surface: An oriental potentate comes back to a sculpture by Jacob Epstein.
explanation.walkthrough: Epstein's carved relief in Hyde Park, London, a memorial to W. H. Hudson, shows the bird-girl from Hudson's novel Green Mansions.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein's controversial 1925 Hyde Park relief is named after the heroine of Hudson's Green Mansions.

clue.text: Concerning new students with a way of retiring for a light meal

parts.note: re means concerning, about
freshmen are first-year university students

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the street abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: First-year students go off to bed in search of a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns ST round to TS, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshments are food and drink served as a snack, a small meal.

clue.text: Live fish ?'

parts.note: not fish still alive but fish that are live in the electrical sense, carrying a charge

explanation.surface: A fishmonger offers fish that are still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'live' wire carries current; these South American fish can stun prey with a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: These South American fish produce powerful shocks, so they are charged like a live wire.

clue.text: Fish swears horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the word swears is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone curses dreadfully, perhaps over a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts.

clue.text: Dangerous company floating?

parts.note: reads like a risky business being floated on the stock market, but describes a perilous group of drifting things at sea

explanation.surface: A hazardous firm is being launched on the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'float' a company is to offer its shares on the market; here the floating group is literal and a menace to shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Great masses of ice drifting at sea are a hazard to ships, the Titanic being the famous victim.

clue.text: Mounted apace

definitions.meaning: mounted means sitting on a horse with a leg either side
read as 'a pace', which is a stride

explanation.surface: Someone on horseback moves quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apace' normally means quickly; split it as 'a pace' and it means a single stride.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits with legs either side of the saddle; and a pace is one step, a stride.

clue.text: Like carrying out alterations to dull cafés?

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the word for like wraps the rest

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: alterations means the letters of out are changed in order

parts.note: mat, also spelt matt, means dull, not glossy

explanation.surface: Someone is making changes to drab cafés.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alterations' turns OUT into UTO; 'carrying' puts AS round UTO and MAT: A-UTOMAT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Automats were American self-service restaurants where food came from coin-operated compartments.

clue.text: So tired of correcting anthologists!

indicators.note: correcting suggests text being amended, so the letters of so tired are rearranged

explanation.surface: Compilers of anthologies are weary of fixing mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correcting' rearranges SO TIRED; the surface fits, since compilers correct texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who compile anthologies select and arrange other writers' work, the job of an editor.

clue.text: Persuade " an" ingenious churchman to take part?

indicators.note: to take part means to be a part of the words before, so the answer is a run inside them

explanation.surface: Coax a clever cleric to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'persuaDE AN INGEnious'. W. R. Inge, Dean of St Paul's, was known as the Gloomy Dean.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ralph Inge was Dean of St Paul's Cathedral from 1911 to 1934, a well-known clergyman and writer.

clue.text: Judge making notes

definitions.meaning: in England a part-time judge of the Crown Court bears this title
one who writes things down, or a wind instrument that produces musical notes

explanation.surface: A judge is jotting things down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Recorder is a type of judge in England; the second sense is a note-taker or the woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorders sit as part-time judges in England; and the woodwind pipe produces musical notes.

clue.text: Hint given by writer on fish

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so the writing fluid sits over the fish

parts.note: ink is what a writer writes with, standing for the writer here
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An author drops a clue about a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts INK above LING.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suspicion or vague notion.

clue.text: Poet revised sonnet about New York

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters wrap the state abbreviation
revised means reworked, so the letters of sonnet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet has rewritten a fourteen-line poem about New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns SONNET into TENSON, and 'about' puts it round NY: TEN-NY-SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Poet Laureate for much of Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Courage still engendered?

definitions.meaning: liquor produced by a distilling still

explanation.surface: Bravery is still being born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like the adverb 'yet'; it is the apparatus for distilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is pluck or mettle; and spirits such as whisky come from a still.

clue.text: Each has a portion

parts.note: a piece is a portion or share

explanation.surface: Everyone gets a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for every one, individually.

clue.text: Song brings back co-belligerents in various armies

indicators.note: in places the reversed word within the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of armies arranged in varied ways
brings back says the word for co-belligerents is read in reverse

parts.note: allies are nations fighting on the same side

explanation.surface: A tune recalls the allied forces among assorted armies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back' turns ALLIES into SEILLA; 'various' rearranges ARMIES into MARISE, and 'in' sets SEILLA inside it: MAR-SEILLA-ISE.
explanation.definitionFit: La Marseillaise is the French national anthem.

clue.text: I'd be the last to bring: this up!

definitions.text: I'd be the last to bring: this up!

parts.words: I'd be the last to bring: this up!
parts.note: the speaker is the hindmost part, and the word also means to raise or bring up

explanation.surface: Someone protests they would never mention the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The rear is the last position; and to rear children is to bring them up.
explanation.definitionFit: The back is the last position, and raising children is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: Little boy in the river ?

definitions.meaning: a pet form of Edward, a little boy's name
a circular swirl of water found in a river

explanation.surface: A small lad is in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a child paddling; the second sense is the whirlpool itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a diminutive of Edward; and a whirling counter-current is found in rivers.

clue.text: Drawing vehicle back in to repair

indicators.note: back says the vehicle is read in reverse

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

indicators.note: repair says the letters of in to are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle is towed back for fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CART into TRAC; 'repair' rearranges IN TO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of pulling or drawing a load.

clue.text: Gunmen in garages ?

parts.note: not armed robbers, but mechanics who wield grease guns to lubricate cars

explanation.surface: Armed men are lurking in the garages.
explanation.walkthrough: A grease gun pumps lubricant into a car's joints, so the garage hand using one is a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanics who lubricate vehicles with grease guns are named after the stuff they apply.
